title: OPERA Vegetation Disturbance Status (DIST-ALERT VEG-DIST-STATUS)
description:
Researchers working with the Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) and Observational Products for End-Users from Remote Sensing Analysis (OPERA) teams at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Pasadena, California, produce the OPERA Land Surface Disturbance Alert (DIST-ALERT) products. Results posted here are preliminary, primarily intended to aid field response, and are provided with absolutely no warranty of any kind. Use at your own risk.
Each image is the VEG-DIST-STATUS layer, which reports the detection status and confidence of vegetation cover loss for each pixel relative to a pre-event baseline. It is a categorical layer, rendered with a discrete colormap and no rescale.
VEG-DIST-STATUS classes:
0 = no disturbance; 1 = first detection, vegetation cover loss < 50%; 2 = provisional detection, < 50%; 3 = confirmed detection, < 50%; 4 = first detection, >= 50%; 5 = provisional detection, >= 50%; 6 = confirmed detection, >= 50%; 7 = confirmed, < 50%, finished; 8 = confirmed, >= 50%, finished; 255 = no data. 'First' is a single anomalous observation with no follow-up yet, 'provisional' is two consecutive detections, 'confirmed' is a high-confidence detection, and 'finished' means the disturbance is no longer being detected.
